payload.text: **THE LAYOUT IS A FLAT SCROLLING COLUMN OF `{title, value, type}` ROWS WITH NO BORDERS AND NO DECORATION, AND THE ONLY FORMATTING GUARANTEE IS COLUMN ALIGNMENT.** Field names align in one column and values align in another, across the whole form -- **that alignment IS the design, so it is asserted rather than eyeballed**: every rendered row has its name starting at one column and its value at another, measured over a form whose longest name and longest value both exceed the viewport. **THE FOOT IS THE RATIFIED DESIGN'S, NOT THIS ROW'S ORIGINAL WORDING.** This row said *one modeline at the foot above a single rule*; `tui-design.md`, ratified by hv on 2026-08-29, specifies FIVE sections separated by TWO rules -- APP ROW, BODY, then STATUS, COMMAND and INFO. **THE DESIGN WINS AND THE ROW IS CORRECTED TO IT** (vc, 2026-08-30, on ic's finding): the design is a day newer, hv drove it against real data, and a criterion that contradicts a ratified design is the criterion being stale rather than the design being wrong. **ic BUILT TO THIS ROW AND WAS RIGHT TO** -- they had read only section 3 and the row is what the register offered them, which is the whole hazard: a stale criterion is indistinguishable from a current one at the point of use. **THIRD INSTANCE OF THE DATED-MEASUREMENT CLASS ON THIS THREAD** after `AC-12.4` and `AC-17.6`, and the first where a row contradicts a ratified artefact rather than merely citing a moved surface -- so the class is not only about staleness in prose, it reaches rows that were never reconciled against a document written after them. **A field whose value does not fit is truncated visibly, never wrapped into a second row**, because a wrapped value breaks the one guarantee the layout makes.
